     Edit the `diagnose` row there and run `npm run macro-skills`. -->

Diagnose the problem below. Your first move is a command that produces evidence, never a
patch.

1. BUILD A LOOP FIRST. Find ONE command — a test, a script, a CLI call with a fixture, a
   ledger query — that goes red on the EXACT symptom reported, not on something nearby.
   Run it and show the invocation and its output. Make it fast and deterministic: pin
   time, seed randomness, narrow the scope. For a flaky failure, raise the reproduction
   rate until it is debuggable. Until this command exists, do not read code to build a
   theory. If you cannot build one, stop and say what you tried and what you need from me.
2. CHECK WHAT CHANGED. "It worked yesterday" outweighs any theory. Read `git log` for the
   area and the dates first. Check that the upstream inputs are what you assume before you
   touch the logic that consumes them. For a pipeline, count items at every step before
   changing any filter.
3. MINIMISE. Cut inputs, config and steps one at a time, re-running the loop after each
   cut, until only the parts that make it fail remain.
4. HYPOTHESISE, RANKED. List the candidate causes. For each, name the one observation that
   would falsify it, and check that observation before you believe it.
5. FIX THE NAMED CAUSE, then re-run the SAME loop and show it green. Prove the fix is
   load-bearing: undo it, show red, restore it, show green.

If two patches have not moved the symptom, stop. No third patch and no wider change — get
more data or return to the last known good state.

Report what you OBSERVED (with the command) separately from what you INFERRED. Redact every
secret from any output you show.

Rules this invokes (CLAUDE.md):

- Investigation discipline
- Coverage traps

$ARGUMENTS
